Data point / insight: Median document submission → first human review
How calculated / source: DOCS_SUBMITTED to REVIEW_STARTED; distinct matched application IDs; median.
What it means: Applicants wait before a human begins reviewing their documents.
Product implication: Run AI validation at upload so common issues are surfaced before the human-review queue.

Data point / insight: Average document submission → first human review
How calculated / source: Mean of the same submission-to-review intervals.
What it means: Average is higher than median, indicating a tail of longer waits.
Product implication: Track median and upper percentiles, not only average.

What it means: 90% began review within this time; 10% waited longer.
Product implication: Use queue-age alerts and escalation for long-wait cases.

What it means: 5% waited longer than this before first review.
Product implication: Prioritise aging applications and exception queues.

What it means: Overall journey is much longer than first-review wait; delays compound across stages.
Product implication: Treat first-review speed as a leading lever; track final certification separately.

What it means: Applicant-level count, not number of correction events.
Product implication: Use as denominator for correction-rate metric.

Data point / insight: Share of started applications returned for corrections
What it means: About one in four started applications had a correction event.
Product implication: Pre-upload checks can prevent avoidable returns.

How calculated / source: Count of DOC_RETURNED rows in stage_events.

Product implication: Consolidate all known issues into one correction request.

What it means: Cross-document consistency issues are a substantial part of corrections.

What it means: Candidates for early automated detection; detection is not automatic resolution.
Product implication: Run validation at upload and show actionable correction instructions.

What it means: Face matching can flag mismatch; borderline cases need human judgement.

Data point / insight: Applicants with exactly one correction event
How calculated / source: 703 application IDs had one DOC_RETURNED event.
What it means: Most corrected applications had one recorded return event.
Product implication: Consolidate all available findings before sending first request.

What it means: Some applicants experience more than one correction event.
Product implication: Batch all issues into one message where possible.

What it means: Quantifies repeat events beyond one per affected applicant.
Product implication: A consolidated message may avoid repeat messaging when all issues are detectable together.

How calculated / source: AUTO_EXPIRED note explicitly says 'No response to document request in 10 days'.
What it means: Applicants timed out after a document request.
Product implication: Use clear instructions, direct upload links and reminders.

What it means: About 27% did not respond within the recorded 10-day window.
Product implication: Reduce effort and confusion through consolidated communication.

How calculated / source: Distinct application IDs with DOC_REUPLOADED event.
What it means: Applicants who submitted at least one replacement document.
Product implication: Make reupload flow simple and identify exactly which file needs replacement.

What it means: Some applicants reuploaded more than once.
Product implication: Support repeat upload and revalidate changed documents without restarting.

How calculated / source: Application IDs with more than one DOC_REUPLOADED event.
What it means: A subset needed multiple upload attempts.
Product implication: Preserve context and re-check only changed documents.

What it means: Shows progression to document submission.
Product implication: Reduce early friction and abandonment before document completion.

What it means: About 74% of started applications recorded KYC verification.
Product implication: Improve upstream validation and exception resolution.

What it means: Shows movement beyond KYC into training.
Product implication: Monitor KYC-to-training conversion separately.

What it means: Shows recorded certification progression.
Product implication: Track certification outcome and reconcile event/status definitions.

Data point / insight: Drop-off between KYC verification and training start
What it means: Largest single drop-off point in the funnel (50.7% of all 951 dropouts); applicants lose momentum during multi-day KYC wait.
Product implication: Instant automated KYC feedback preserves applicant intent and immediately routes verified agents into training.
Evidence type / caveat: Dataset-derived; status = DROPPED with kyc_verified_at populated.

Data point / insight: Conversion rate from training start to certification
What it means: Once an applicant starts training, virtually 100% complete it and get certified; training and exam are not the bottleneck.
Product implication: All acquisition optimization should focus on removing friction in the pre-training document review window.

Data point / insight: Total reviewer touches and ops expenditure (Jan–Sep)
How calculated / source: 9,920 manual touches across 22 reviewers; 21 min/touch; loaded cost ₹430/hr (mean of ops_team).
What it means: Manual review is cost-heavy (3.31 touches/app) and scales linearly with applicant volume.
Product implication: Automating 60% of cases straight-through and cutting review time to <5 min saves ~₹12+ Lakhs annually.
Evidence type / caveat: Derived from applications.manual_touches and ops_team loaded rates.

What it means: Nearly a quarter of all rejections are due to existing registration with another broker.
Product implication: Move IRDAI registry check to Step 0 (upon typing PAN) before document upload to save applicant effort and reviewer capacity.

Data point / insight: Potential Straight-Through Processing (STP) rate in test set
How calculated / source: application_truth.final_decision == 'APPROVE' (364/600); 268 exact matches + 96 valid rulebook name variants.
What it means: Over 60% of applications satisfy all rulebook criteria without requiring any discretionary human judgment.
Product implication: Meeting the brief's target of ≥60% zero-human-touch STP is mathematically and operationally feasible.

Data point / insight: Reviewer verdict error rate on documents
How calculated / source: Document review test set README and specimen notes.
What it means: Human reviewers make subjective, inconsistent decisions on legitimate name variations (initials, swapped names, spelling).
Product implication: AI rule engine enforces uniform regulatory compliance and removes individual reviewer bias.
Evidence type / caveat: Documented data pack baseline error rate.
